answer.location_description: Small 3x3 square near the top-left corner of the image, rows 1-3, columns 1-3.
answer.mechanism: Two groups of first-layer units read the patch. Units 1, 3, 7, 8, 13, 24, 27 and 28 have strong positive weights there (+50 to +93), and units 18 and 20 are broadly positive with especially large weights there. Units 11, 12, 16, 17, 19, 21, 25, 26 and 29 (and weakly 31) have strong negative weights there (-50 to -99) on top of high biases. In layer 2, u1 (output weight +91) and u0 (+63) take positive input from the patch-positive units (e.g. u1 gets +91 from h28, +76 from h27, +70 from h3) and negative input from the patch-negative units (u1 gets -78 from h25, -65 from h29). u9 (output weight -83) is driven by the patch-negative units (+99 from h26, +88 from h21, +82 from h25, +75 from h16) and inhibited by h1 (-83). A bright patch therefore raises u0/u1 and silences u9, pushing the logit toward class 1 (large blob).
answer.evidence: The patch is the most conspicuous structure in the first-layer weights: a sharply bounded 3x3 block at r1-r3, c1-c3 whose weights have magnitude roughly 45-99, far above the surrounding values (about ±30). It shows up with a consistent sign in about 20 of the 32 hidden units. The sign tracks each unit's blob-size role: units that favour a large central disk/ring (1, 3, 7, 8, 13, 24, 27, 28) are positive on the patch. Units that are negative on the centre and positive on the surround, i.e. small-blob/background detectors (11, 12, 16, 17, 19, 21, 25, 26, 29), are negative on the patch. Following these weights through layer 2 to the output gives a net push toward class 1. A blob centred in the image could not explain a feature isolated in the corner.
answer.main_feature: Blob size is read from ring/disk templates over the centre (roughly rows 5-18, columns 5-18). Units whose positive weights extend out to a large radius signal a large blob. Units with a negative centre and positive surround fire when the bright area is small, signalling a small blob.
